A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same preference-optimization framework for CLIP. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching relocated ImageNet results and renumbered ablations.

before.justification: V1 reports original typographic classification experiments, gender-control and retrieval results, and hyperparameter, averaging and sample-efficiency studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds projection diagnostics, policy-ratio distributions and CIFAR-10 adversarial-robustness results.

M1.justification: Appendix K.1 adds online generation of targeted PGD adversarial examples during training, a procedural adaptation of the existing preference framework. The DPO/IPO/KTO objectives, regularization, BMA and SVD-based head remain unchanged. New Algorithm 1 summarizes the existing optimization procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 training and evaluation under targeted PGD pixel perturbations, extending robustness coverage to a substantially different attack scenario beyond misleading text. Existing typographic, gender-control and FOOD101/SUN coverage remains; the ImageNet reorganization does not establish an additional task.

E2.justification: V1 Table 1 compares ImageNet results against CLIP, Materzynska+, PAINT and Defense-Prefix; v2's corresponding Table 4 retains only CLIP. Comparator membership on the other typographic benchmarks is unchanged. ROPO additionally appears in a weighting-function illustration, without reported benchmark accuracy.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an online PGD training protocol with epsilon 2/255 and 4/255, reporting respectively 1000 and 700 iterations with batch size 256. Section 4.1.1 expands transformation scaling from [-2, 1.2] to [-4, 4]. The revised ImageNet comparison also supplies a subset-specific CLIP control; retained experiments keep their original core settings.

E4.justification: New analyses examine projection orthogonality and singular values (Appendix E), weighting functions and policy-ratio distributions across datasets (Appendix J), and PGD robustness (Appendix K). Figure 2 extends scaling sensitivity. V1's hyperparameter, BMA/EMA and sample-efficiency studies remain in v2 Appendices G–I rather than being new experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 0 and retain the same KL-divergence boxplots. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure. Its new policy-ratio distributions describe variation across examples rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds projection and policy-ratio findings, revised Figure 2 curves, and CIFAR-10 adversarial/clean accuracies of 62.89%/98.44% at epsilon 2/255 and 21.88%/97.27% at 4/255. Shared typographic scores remain unchanged, but Table 1 adds averages and revises differences. StanfordCars' clean difference changes from -0.96 to +0.9 despite unchanged KTO/CLIP scores of 57.76/58.72. ImageNet CLIP values are replaced by 54.21/33.23 for the clarified subset; this is not a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces derivations relating similarity distortion and transformed embedding norms to ||W^T W - I|| in Equations 35–36. The existing MDP formulation, preference objectives, lemmas, gradient expressions and Appendix B proofs are retained apart from numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion explicitly foreground comparison of DPO, IPO and KTO. The conclusion removes v1's claim about handling race, narrowing the sensitive-attribute claim to gender. The central claims about typographic robustness, concept control and knowledge retention remain.

C2.justification: Appendix J adds explanations attributing KTO's sample efficiency to splitting preference triplets and IPO's beta sensitivity to policy flattening, alongside interpretations of gradient weights and dataset-specific strengths. Section 3.4 and Appendix E qualify extreme scaling through normalization concerns. Appendix F explicitly discusses applicability without human-curated preferences.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, identifies the ImageNetV2 matched-frequency subset, explains KTO's conversion of triplets into binary examples, and supplies budgets for the new PGD experiment. Its normalization guidance also expands implementation documentation. Existing hardware, optimizer and BMA details were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liang et al.'s ROPO reference and expands discussion of existing baselines. Appendix E contrasts preference optimization's implicit proximity with Materzynska et al.'s explicit orthogonality regularization. Several other reference changes consolidate duplicate entries rather than change the cited research.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized edits to the abstract, contributions, regularization explanation and conclusion, standardizes terminology, and expands baseline explanations. It adds a main-text algorithm summary and appendix sections while retaining the main narrative order and most existing theoretical and experimental prose.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces ImageNet columns with averages and separates ImageNet results into Table 4. Figure 2 is redrawn with wider axes. V2 adds orthogonality displays, weighting and policy-ratio plots, PGD training curves and Table 7. Existing figures and ablations are also relocated or receive caption and panel-layout refinements.

improvement.justification: Separating the mismatched ImageNet comparison and adding direct orthogonality diagnostics address weaknesses in v1; the code link also improves reproducibility information. These gains are limited by incomplete PGD evaluation details and errors introduced in Table 1's revised differences, including StanfordCars' unsupported +0.9. The revision provides a useful but qualified improvement in evidential support and clarity.
